**Annabella Avery Thorne** (born October 8, 1997) is an American actress, singer, and writer. She first received recognition for her roles as Margaux Darling in the series _Dirty Sexy Money_ (2007–2008) and as Ruthy Spivey in the drama series _My Own Worst Enemy_ (2009), the latter of which earned her a Young Artist Award.
Thorne gained prominence for her role as CeCe Jones on the Disney Channel series _Shake It Up_ (2010–2013), for which she received several awards and nominations, including winning an Imagen Award.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bella_Thorne#cite_note-2) Thorne has since appeared in numerous feature films, including _Blended_ (2014), _Alvin and the Chipmunks: The Road Chip_ (2015), _The Babysitter_ and its sequel (2017–2020). She received praise for her roles in _The DUFF_ (2015), _Amityville: The Awakening_ (2017), and _Infamous_ (2020). Thorne also led the drama series _Famous in Love_ (2017–2018), for which she received nominations from the Teen Choice Awards.

Outside of acting, Thorne has ventured into music; she released her debut single, "Watch Me" in 2011, which charted at No. 86 on the US _Billboard_ Hot 100. She has since released the EP _Made in Japan_ in 2012 and the EP _Jersey_ in 2014. She made her directorial debut in 2019, directing the pornographic film_Her & Him_, which garnered positive reviews and won a Pornhub Visionary Award.

## Early life
Annabella Avery Thorne[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bella_Thorne#cite_note-AllMusic_Bio-3) was born on October 8, 1997, in Pembroke Pines, Florida,[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bella_Thorne#cite_note-UPI-1)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bella_Thorne#cite_note-Allmusic-4)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bella_Thorne#cite_note-Chase's_p502-5) the daughter of Tamara Thorne and Delancey Reinaldo "Rey" Thorne.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bella_Thorne#cite_note-Disney_Channel_Medianet-6)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bella_Thorne#cite_note-7) She has three siblings who are also actors.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bella_Thorne#cite_note-Disney_Channel_Medianet-6)[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bella_Thorne#cite_note-TVG-8) Her father, who was of Cuban descent,[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bella_Thorne#cite_note-HuffPo-ShakeItUp-2012-9)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bella_Thorne#cite_note-InTouchWeekly-AboutDyingAlone-2017-10)[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bella_Thorne#cite_note-USWeekly-AutumnFalls-2014-11) died in a traffic accident in April 2007, when Thorne was nine years old.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bella_Thorne#cite_note-SunSentinel-Father-Obit-2007-12)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bella_Thorne#cite_note-MiamiHerald-AutumnFalls-2014-13) She has said that she was raised by a mother who was supporting four children, that they were very poor,

## Early life
and that she originally began working as a child actress to help support the family.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bella_Thorne#cite_note-14)
In September 2017, Thorne revealed that she had lived in a suburban area, spoke Spanish as her first language, and that she was bullied while growing up because she was dyslexic.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bella_Thorne#cite_note-HarpersBazaar-FamousInLove-2017-15)[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bella_Thorne#cite_note-ChelseaShow-2017-16) She was diagnosed with dyslexia while in first grade. She was home-schooled after previously attending a public school, where she had been bullied. She improved in her learning after attending a Sylvan Learning center and began reading and writing a grade ahead.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bella_Thorne#cite_note-Film_Monthly.com-17) In April 2010, she said she had overcome dyslexia by rigorously reading everything she could find, including cereal box labels.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bella_Thorne#cite_note-American_Cheerleader_Magazine-18)[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bella_Thorne#cite_note-OceanUp.com_2-19)
In January 2018, Thorne wrote on Instagram that she had been physically and sexually abused as a child, "from the day I can remember till I was 14".[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bella_Thorne#cite_note-20) In 2019, she told ABC News' Juju Chang that the abuse began when she was six years old. She did not name her alleged abuser, but said that he was "someone I was raised with".[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bella_Thorne#cite_note-21)

## Career
### 2003–2009: Early work and acting beginnings
Thorne's first film appearance was an uncredited role as a sidelines fan in the 2003 film _Stuck on You_. She has since appeared in film and television projects including _Entourage_ and _[The O.C.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_O.C. "The O.C.")_ as a younger version of Taylor Townsend. In 2007, she joined the recurring cast of _Dirty Sexy Money_'s second season as Margaux Darling. This is her first major television role. The series revolves around lawyer and family man Nick George; when Nick's father mysteriously dies in a plane crash, he agrees to take his position as the Darling family's lawyer, while trying to discover who committed the murder.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bella_Thorne#cite_note-Bella_Thorne_Interview-22)
In 2008, Thorne starred alongside Christian Slater and Taylor Lautner in the short-lived drama series _My Own Worst Enemy_, for which she won a Young Artist Award for her portrayal of the character Ruthy Spivey; Thorne described her _Enemy_ casting as a major breakthrough as this was the first recurring role in her career. The same year, she starred in the third-last episode of _October Road_ as Angela Ferilli, the pre-adolescence crush of the main characters. Her older brother Remy also guest-starred in the same episode as a younger Eddie Latekka._[citation needed_]
In 2009, she starred in the web series _Little Monk_, which depicted characters from the series _Monk_, as Wendy, one of Adrian Monk's classmates. The webisodes are available only on the "Best of Monk" DVD. Also in 2009, she played the role of the vengeful antagonist in the horror film _Forget Me Not_. Thorne took on a supporting role in the family drama _Raspberry Magic_, which premiered at the Cinequest Film Festival[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bella_Thorne#cite_note-23) and the San Francisco International Asian American Film Festival in 2010.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bella_Thorne#cite_note-24)

## Career
### 2010–2013: Breakthrough with Disney and music
Thorne and Zendaya at a promotional event for _Shake It Up_ in 2011
Thorne at the 2013 Movieguide Awards
In 2010, Thorne replaced Jolean Wejbe as Tancy "Teenie" Henrickson, Bill and Barb Henrickson's younger daughter, in Season 4 of HBO's _Big Love_.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bella_Thorne#cite_note-25) Thorne co-starred on the Disney Channel sitcom _Shake It Up_, originally titled _Dance, Dance Chicago_. Thorne played CeCe Jones, a dancer with ambitions for a career in the spotlight despite having dyslexia.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bella_Thorne#cite_note-Variety.com-26) The show is a buddy comedy centered on a teen dance show (in a show-within-a-show format) co-starring Thorne and Zendaya.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bella_Thorne#cite_note-OceanUp.com-27) The multi-camera series began production in Hollywood, California, in July 2010 and premiered on November 7, 2010, on Disney Channel. While she had a substantial portfolio of work in television and film, Thorne had no experience in professional dancing before being cast. After signing onto the show in October 2009, she began taking three dance classes every night.

## Career
### 2010–2013: Breakthrough with Disney and music
Thorne's first single, "Watch Me" was released on June 21, reaching 86 on the US _Billboard_ Hot 100 charts,[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bella_Thorne#cite_note-Allmusic-4) 9 on the US Top Heatseekers charts[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bella_Thorne#cite_note-28) and earning RIAA: Gold.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bella_Thorne#cite_note-29) On September 29, 2011, Disney Channel announced it had increased _Shake It Up_'s second season order to 26 episodes.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bella_Thorne#cite_note-30) A 90-minute special episode _Made In Japan_ aired August 17, 2012, as the season two finale.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bella_Thorne#cite_note-31) On June 4, 2012, Disney Channel announced that _Shake It Up_ had been renewed for a third season.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bella_Thorne#cite_note-DCPRS3-32) In 2012, Thorne was cast as Avalon Greene in the Disney Channel Original Movie_Frenemies_.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bella_Thorne#cite_note-33) "TTYLXOX" was released on March 6, reaching 97 on the US _Billboard_ Hot 100 charts.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bella_Thorne#cite_note-bill-34) On March 30, 2013, it was confirmed by Hollywood Records via Twitter that Thorne had officially signed to the record label.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bella_Thorne#cite_note-35)

## Career
### 2010–2013: Breakthrough with Disney and music
On July 25, 2013, Disney Channel confirmed that _Shake It Up_ would be canceled after the show's third season.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bella_Thorne#cite_note-36)[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bella_Thorne#cite_note-37) On April 23, 2013, Thorne announced her debut album with eleven songs.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bella_Thorne#cite_note-38)[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bella_Thorne#cite_note-dancingqueen219_says:_I'm_not_a_big_fan_of_her_music-39) Thorne spoke about the album, saying "What fans can expect is [for it] just to be very different from anyone because I don't like to be one of those artists where you can be like: 'Oh yeah, I know them from that song.' All my songs are very different from each other. So [I don't want to be](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I_Don't_Want_to_Be "I Don't Want to Be") known as only one genre."[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bella_Thorne#cite_note-dancingqueen219_says:_I'm_not_a_big_fan_of_her_music-39) Thorne cited Britney Spears, Kesha, and [Destiny's Child](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Destiny's_Child "Destiny's Child") as influences for the album.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bella_Thorne#cite_note-contactmusic-40)[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bella_Thorne#cite_note-41) In 2013, it was reported that Thorne had signed a new deal to write a series of books, beginning with her first novel, _Autumn Falls_.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bella_Thorne#cite_note-42)

## Career
### 2014–2017: Mainstream film and television
In 2014, Thorne co-starred in the comedy _Blended_, as Adam Sandler's character's daughter.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bella_Thorne#cite_note-43) She also co-starred in the films _Alexander and the Terrible, Horrible, No Good, Very Bad Day_ (2014) and _The DUFF_ (2015), playing high school antagonists.[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bella_Thorne#cite_note-44) On July 30, Thorne was cast in an episode of the fifteenth season of the _CSI: Crime Scene Investigation_.[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bella_Thorne#cite_note-45) The episode, "The Book of Shadows", aired October 19, 2014.[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bella_Thorne#cite_note-46) Thorne appeared in the sequel to _Mostly Ghostly_ (2008), titled _Mostly Ghostly: Have You Met My Ghoulfriend_ (2014) as Cammy Cahill.[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bella_Thorne#cite_note-47) On October 15, Thorne revealed her debut album was canceled, saying she wasn't happy with the "auto-tuned bad music" she had in the works.[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bella_Thorne#cite_note-48) She released an EP, _Jersey_, on November 17.[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bella_Thorne#cite_note-49)[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bella_Thorne#cite_note-50) The lead single from the EP, "Call It Whatever", debuted in the _Billboard_Hot Dance Club Songs chart at number forty-seven, eventually rising to number ten,

## Career
### 2014–2017: Mainstream film and television
spending a total of ten weeks on the chart.[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bella_Thorne#cite_note-Billboard-51)[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bella_Thorne#cite_note-HotClub-52)[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bella_Thorne#cite_note-53) Thorne has signed on as one of the leads in Manis Film's thriller _Big Sky_;
in which she plays Hazel.[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bella_Thorne#cite_note-deadlinesky-54) In 2014, Thorne was cast in the MTV series _Scream_, which is a television adaptation based on the original slasher film series _Scream_.[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bella_Thorne#cite_note-BellaThorneCasted-55) Thorne was offered the lead role of the series but felt that the role of the "mean, terrible Nina" would be more iconic.[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bella_Thorne#cite_note-56)
Thorne at the premiere of _Divergent_ in April 2014

She improved in her learning after attending a Sylvan Learning center and began reading and writing a grade ahead.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bella_Thorne#cite_note-Film_Monthly.com-17) In April 2010, she said she had overcome dyslexia by rigorously reading everything she could find, including cereal box labels.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bella_Thorne#cite_note-American_Cheerleader_Magazine-18)[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bella_Thorne#cite_note-OceanUp.com_2-19)
In January 2018, Thorne wrote on Instagram that she had been physically and sexually abused as a child, "from the day I can remember till I was 14".[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bella_Thorne#cite_note-20) In 2019, she told ABC News' Juju Chang that the abuse began when she was six years old. She did not name her alleged abuser, but said that he was "someone I was raised with".[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bella_Thorne#cite_note-21)
texts.4:
## Career
### 2003–2009: Early work and acting beginnings
Thorne's first film appearance was an uncredited role as a sidelines fan in the 2003 film _Stuck on You_. She has since appeared in film and television projects including _Entourage_ and _[The O.C.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_O.C. "The O.C.")_ as a younger version of Taylor Townsend. In 2007, she joined the recurring cast of _Dirty Sexy Money_'s second season as Margaux Darling. This is her first major television role. The series revolves around lawyer and family man Nick George; when Nick's father mysteriously dies in a plane crash, he agrees to take his position as the Darling family's lawyer, while trying to discover who committed the murder.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bella_Thorne#cite_note-Bella_Thorne_Interview-22)
In 2008, Thorne starred alongside Christian Slater and Taylor Lautner in the short-lived drama series _My Own Worst Enemy_, for which she won a Young Artist Award for her portrayal of the character Ruthy Spivey; Thorne described her _Enemy_ casting as a major breakthrough as this was the first recurring role in her career. The same year, she starred in the third-last episode of _October Road_ as Angela Ferilli, the pre-adolescence crush of the main characters. Her older brother Remy also guest-starred in the same episode as a younger Eddie Latekka._[citation needed_]
In 2009, she starred in the web series _Little Monk_, which depicted characters from the series _Monk_, as Wendy, one of Adrian Monk's classmates. The webisodes are available only on the "Best of Monk" DVD. Also in 2009, she played the role of the vengeful antagonist in the horror film _Forget Me Not_. Thorne took on a supporting role in the family drama _Raspberry Magic_, which premiered at the Cinequest Film Festival[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bella_Thorne#cite_note-23) and the San Francisco International Asian American Film Festival in 2010.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bella_Thorne#cite_note-24)
texts.5:
## Career
### 2010–2013: Breakthrough with Disney and music
Thorne and Zendaya at a promotional event for _Shake It Up_ in 2011
Thorne at the 2013 Movieguide Awards
In 2010, Thorne replaced Jolean Wejbe as Tancy "Teenie" Henrickson, Bill and Barb Henrickson's younger daughter, in Season 4 of HBO's _Big Love_.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bella_Thorne#cite_note-25) Thorne co-starred on the Disney Channel sitcom _Shake It Up_, originally titled _Dance, Dance Chicago_. Thorne played CeCe Jones, a dancer with ambitions for a career in the spotlight despite having dyslexia.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bella_Thorne#cite_note-Variety.com-26) The show is a buddy comedy centered on a teen dance show (in a show-within-a-show format) co-starring Thorne and Zendaya.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bella_Thorne#cite_note-OceanUp.com-27) The multi-camera series began production in Hollywood, California, in July 2010 and premiered on November 7, 2010, on Disney Channel. While she had a substantial portfolio of work in television and film, Thorne had no experience in professional dancing before being cast. After signing onto the show in October 2009, she began taking three dance classes every night.
texts.6:
## Career
### 2010–2013: Breakthrough with Disney and music
Thorne's first single, "Watch Me" was released on June 21, reaching 86 on the US _Billboard_ Hot 100 charts,[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bella_Thorne#cite_note-Allmusic-4) 9 on the US Top Heatseekers charts[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bella_Thorne#cite_note-28) and earning RIAA: Gold.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bella_Thorne#cite_note-29) On September 29, 2011, Disney Channel announced it had increased _Shake It Up_'s second season order to 26 episodes.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bella_Thorne#cite_note-30) A 90-minute special episode _Made In Japan_ aired August 17, 2012, as the season two finale.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bella_Thorne#cite_note-31) On June 4, 2012, Disney Channel announced that _Shake It Up_ had been renewed for a third season.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bella_Thorne#cite_note-DCPRS3-32) In 2012, Thorne was cast as Avalon Greene in the Disney Channel Original Movie_Frenemies_.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bella_Thorne#cite_note-33) "TTYLXOX" was released on March 6, reaching 97 on the US _Billboard_ Hot 100 charts.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bella_Thorne#cite_note-bill-34) On March 30, 2013, it was confirmed by Hollywood Records via Twitter that Thorne had officially signed to the record label.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bella_Thorne#cite_note-35)
texts.7:
## Career
### 2010–2013: Breakthrough with Disney and music
On July 25, 2013, Disney Channel confirmed that _Shake It Up_ would be canceled after the show's third season.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bella_Thorne#cite_note-36)[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bella_Thorne#cite_note-37) On April 23, 2013, Thorne announced her debut album with eleven songs.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bella_Thorne#cite_note-38)[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bella_Thorne#cite_note-dancingqueen219_says:_I'm_not_a_big_fan_of_her_music-39) Thorne spoke about the album, saying "What fans can expect is [for it] just to be very different from anyone because I don't like to be one of those artists where you can be like: 'Oh yeah, I know them from that song.' All my songs are very different from each other. So [I don't want to be](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I_Don't_Want_to_Be "I Don't Want to Be") known as only one genre."[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bella_Thorne#cite_note-dancingqueen219_says:_I'm_not_a_big_fan_of_her_music-39) Thorne cited Britney Spears, Kesha, and [Destiny's Child](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Destiny's_Child "Destiny's Child") as influences for the album.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bella_Thorne#cite_note-contactmusic-40)[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bella_Thorne#cite_note-41) In 2013, it was reported that Thorne had signed a new deal to write a series of books, beginning with her first novel, _Autumn Falls_.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bella_Thorne#cite_note-42)
texts.8:
## Career
### 2014–2017: Mainstream film and television
In 2014, Thorne co-starred in the comedy _Blended_, as Adam Sandler's character's daughter.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bella_Thorne#cite_note-43) She also co-starred in the films _Alexander and the Terrible, Horrible, No Good, Very Bad Day_ (2014) and _The DUFF_ (2015), playing high school antagonists.[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bella_Thorne#cite_note-44) On July 30, Thorne was cast in an episode of the fifteenth season of the _CSI: Crime Scene Investigation_.[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bella_Thorne#cite_note-45) The episode, "The Book of Shadows", aired October 19, 2014.[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bella_Thorne#cite_note-46) Thorne appeared in the sequel to _Mostly Ghostly_ (2008), titled _Mostly Ghostly: Have You Met My Ghoulfriend_ (2014) as Cammy Cahill.[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bella_Thorne#cite_note-47) On October 15, Thorne revealed her debut album was canceled, saying she wasn't happy with the "auto-tuned bad music" she had in the works.[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bella_Thorne#cite_note-48) She released an EP, _Jersey_, on November 17.[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bella_Thorne#cite_note-49)[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bella_Thorne#cite_note-50) The lead single from the EP, "Call It Whatever", debuted in the _Billboard_Hot Dance Club Songs chart at number forty-seven, eventually rising to number ten,

American singer Bella Thorne has released two extended plays, seven singles, six featured singles, four promotional singles, and sixteen music videos. Thorne's first single, "Watch Me", was released on June 21 featuring Zendaya and reaching 86 on the United States _Billboard_ Hot 100 charts.[[1]](https://officialbellathorne.fandom.com/wiki/Bella_Thorne_discography#cite_note-1) 9 on the US Top Heatseekers charts[[2]](https://officialbellathorne.fandom.com/wiki/Bella_Thorne_discography#cite_note-2) and earning RIAA: Gold.[[3]](https://officialbellathorne.fandom.com/wiki/Bella_Thorne_discography#cite_note-riaa-3) The second single, "TTYLXOX", was released on March 6, reaching 97 on the US _Billboard_ Hot 100 charts.[[4]](https://officialbellathorne.fandom.com/wiki/Bella_Thorne_discography#cite_note-hot100-4)
In March 2013, Bella Thorne announced she'd been signed to Hollywood Records, and began working on her debut material.[[5]](https://officialbellathorne.fandom.com/wiki/Bella_Thorne_discography#cite_note-5) On May 2, 2014 it was revealed her debut album is titled _Call It Whatever_[[6]](https://officialbellathorne.fandom.com/wiki/Bella_Thorne_discography#cite_note-6) and, in May 14, she released her debut single "Call It Whatever".[[7]](https://officialbellathorne.fandom.com/wiki/Bella_Thorne_discography#cite_note-Billboard-7) On October 15, Thorne revealed her debut album was canceled and she releaseed an EP, _Jersey_, on November 17,2014.[[8]](https://officialbellathorne.fandom.com/wiki/Bella_Thorne_discography#cite_note-8)
